claims.text: MetalLB runs in the namespace metallb-system as a controller (a Deployment, one Pod) and a speaker on every node (a DaemonSet, one Pod per node).
claims.source_hint: metallb.io: Concepts (controller, speaker); Installation by manifest; outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/metallb-install.txt

claims.text: MetalLB's controller watches LoadBalancer Services, assigns each an unused address from an IPAddressPool and writes it into .status.loadBalancer.ingress, which kubectl shows as EXTERNAL-IP instead of <pending>.
claims.source_hint: metallb.io: Concepts (Address allocation); kubernetes.io Services > type: LoadBalancer (.status.loadBalancer)

claims.text: Speakers announce an assigned address only if an L2Advertisement covers its pool; lab-pool's does by naming it. Without one, the address is assigned but not announced. One node answers for each address, so other machines send its packets to that node.
claims.source_hint: metallb.io: Configuration > Layer 2 configuration ('no advertisement ... not announced'); Concepts > Layer 2

claims.text: MetalLB speakers do not announce Service addresses from nodes labelled node.kubernetes.io/exclude-from-external-load-balancers; on donhang only the control-plane node carries that label, yet a speaker Pod still runs there.

Traffic to the address reaches the announcing node, where kube-proxy forwards it to a ready Pod on that node or another, as for a node port (externalTrafficPolicy Cluster); MetalLB is not in the request path.
claims.source_hint: metallb.io: Concepts > Layer 2 ('kube-proxy spreads traffic'; not a load balancer in the data path); kubernetes.io Virtual IPs and Service Proxies

claims.text: A LoadBalancer Service that receives an external address keeps its cluster IP and its node port.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Services > type: LoadBalancer (builds on NodePort/ClusterIP); outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/metallb-pool.txt

claims.text: MetalLB hands out only addresses listed in pools and cannot see which addresses other machines use. For the announcements an L2Advertisement asks for, the pool must be on the nodes' own network and used by nothing else.
claims.source_hint: metallb.io: Concepts ('MetalLB cannot create IP addresses out of thin air, so you do have to give it pools'); Configuration > IPAddressPool

claims.text: On a real network you should reserve the pool's range with whoever hands out addresses there, when the network also has other machines that receive addresses.
claims.source_hint: outline item 3; metallb.io: Concepts (pools); conditioned on a shared network

claims.text: scripts/k8s/metallb-install.sh applies deploy/metallb/metallb-native.yaml, a pinned copy of MetalLB 0.15.3's published manifest (namespace, MetalLB's object kinds such as IPAddressPool, controller, speaker), then waits with kubectl rollout status for both.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang scripts/k8s/metallb-install.sh @ stage-3 (header, lines with kubectl apply and rollout status)

claims.text: Captured run of metallb-install.sh: one controller Pod and three speaker Pods (donhang-control-plane and both workers), all ready true; the label query lists only node/donhang-control-plane.
metallb-pool.yaml lines 7-26: IPAddressPool lab-pool in metallb-system with addresses x.y.255.200-x.y.255.250 (51 addresses) and an L2Advertisement lab-pool listing lab-pool under ipAddressPools.
IPAddressPool spec.addresses accepts a range written first-last (as well as CIDR blocks).
claims.source_hint: metallb.io: Configuration > Defining the IPs to assign (addresses: '192.168.10.0/24', '192.168.9.1-192.168.9.5')

claims.text: In the lab run the pool (x.y.255.200-250) sits far above the addresses Docker gave the nodes and containers on kind (172.22.0.x, e.g. 'saw 172.22.0.3'). Observed in the capture only; no general statement about Docker's allocation.

metallb-pool.sh reads kind's /16 IPv4 subnet (all addresses sharing the first two numbers) with docker network inspect (line 14), sed swaps x.y. for those numbers, pipes to kubectl apply -f -, then checks .status.loadBalancer.ingress[0].ip once a second, up to 60 times.

Captured run of metallb-pool.sh: subnet 172.22.0.0/16, pool 172.22.255.200-172.22.255.250 with AUTO ASSIGN true, echo-loadbalancer EXTERNAL-IP 172.22.255.202 with CLUSTER-IP and node port masked, reply 'echo-ip-...-... saw 172.22.0.3'.

Docker Desktop does not connect (route) the host machine to a Docker network such as kind, so a browser on the host gets no answer from the LoadBalancer address, while a container attached to kind (donhang-lb-client) reaches it.
claims.source_hint: docs.docker.com: Docker Desktop networking ('cannot reach container IPs from the host'); STAGE.md @ stage-3 cluster section; metallb-pool.sh lines 34-37

claims.text: metallb-pool.sh runs metallb-install.sh when the namespace metallb-system does not exist; re-applying an unchanged manifest makes kubectl apply report 'unchanged'.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang scripts/k8s/metallb-pool.sh line 9 @ stage-3; kubernetes.io kubectl apply (declarative object management)

claims.text: If a machine outside MetalLB's control is given an address from the pool, two machines claim that address on the network, and calls to the Service may reach the other machine instead.
claims.source_hint: metallb.io: Concepts > Layer 2 (node answers for the address on the local network); general IP address conflict behaviour
